077.t: Testing: Normal, Boundary and Invalid Data
o: Choose normal and boundary tests for a specified allowed input range.
Distinguish invalid values from erroneous data types.
Predict expected test results and identify iterative and final testing.
c: Normal test data is an ordinary valid input, such as mark 50 in an integer mark range 0–100.
Boundary tests cover limits and adjacent values. For range 0–100 inclusive, 0 and 100 are valid; -1 and 101 are outside the range.
Invalid data has the correct type but an unacceptable value, e.g. integer 101 where 0–100 is required. Erroneous data has the wrong type, e.g. the text 'hello' in an integer mark field.
Iterative testing happens during development and after changes. Final (terminal) testing checks the completed solution. Each test case needs an input, expected result and actual result.

m.title: Worked test plan · mark 0–100
m.q: A form accepts integer marks 0–100 inclusive. Give one normal input, two valid boundary inputs, one invalid integer and one erroneous input, with expected outcomes. [5 marks]
st: Normal: 50 is an ordinary integer value and should be Accepted. [1]
Boundaries: 0 and 100 are valid and must both be Accepted. [2]
Invalid: 101 is an integer but out of range; the program should Reject it. [1]
Erroneous: 'hello' has the wrong type; the program should report a type error or ask again before comparing numbers. [1]

w: A ticket program accepts integer quantities from 1 to 20. Give one normal test value and its expected result. [2 marks]
10 is typical normal data [1] and should be Accepted [1].
An age program accepts integers from 11 to 18 inclusive. Give both valid boundaries and one adjacent invalid integer. [2 marks]
Valid boundaries: 11 and 18 [1]; invalid integer: 10 or 19 [1].
A sports score must be an integer 0–100. Classify 120 and 'ten', give their outcomes, and explain when iterative testing happens. [4 marks]

120 is invalid (out-of-range integer), so reject [1]; 'ten' is erroneous text, so report a type error or re-prompt [1]; iterative testing occurs as parts are developed [1] and after changes to check fixes [1].
wSteps: 10 is normal and should be Accepted [2].
Compare wrong value with wrong type.
Iterative testing takes place during development and after changes [2].
Reject 120 [1]; type-error/re-prompt 'ten' [1]; iterative testing in development and after changes [2].

k.q: Trace the OCR ERL program, test a new input and improve the code.
k.code:
mark = 100
if mark >= 0 AND mark <= 100 then
    print("Accepted")
else
    print("Rejected")
endif
p: Predict the initial output when mark is 100.
Run valid and invalid integers -1, 0, 50, 100 and 101; list their expected outputs.
Explain why 'hello' is ERRONEOUS, not an invalid integer. Do not pass text into numeric comparisons without validating type first.
k.a: 100 is Accepted. -1 and 101 are Rejected; 0, 50 and 100 are Accepted. 'hello' is a string instead of an integer: check its type at input and report a clear error or re-prompt before numeric comparisons.

e:
For a program accepting integer marks 0–100, classify input 101 and input 'hello'. [2 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past paper.
101 is invalid: an integer but outside the permitted range [1]. 'hello' is erroneous: a string where an integer is required [1].

A club accepts integer attendance 1–30. Give two valid boundary values, one invalid integer and one erroneous input, with expected outcomes. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past paper.
1 and 30 are valid boundaries (both Accepted) [2]; integer 0 or 31 is invalid (Rejected) [1]; text 'thirty' is erroneous (type error/re-prompt) [1].

A form accepts integer quantities 1–20 inclusive. Give six test cases: one normal, two valid boundaries, one invalid below, one invalid above and one erroneous type. State each expected result. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past paper.
Normal 10 → Accepted [1]; boundaries 1 → Accepted and 20 → Accepted [2]; invalid 0 → Rejected and 21 → Rejected [2]; erroneous 'ten' → type error/re-prompt [1].
v: Input at, just below or just above an allowed limit.
Correct type, unacceptable value, such as integer 101 outside range 0–100.
Wrong type, such as text when an integer is required.
Testing individual program parts during development and after changes.
Testing the completed solution against its requirements.
x: Text 'hello' supplied to an integer-only input is erroneous test data rather than a valid integer.

Explain how range check and authentication help in a school trip form. [4 marks]

Range check [1]; Tests whether a numeric value is between minimum and maximum limits. [1]. Authentication [1]; Checks identity, for example using username and password, rather than checking input format. [1].
